process_area.title: Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics

value_stream.name: Employee Accommodation, Dormitory & Staff Housing Operations

fields.Participants: Facilities (VS-138), Maintenance Vendor/Technician, Housing Ops, HSE (VS-24), Asset (VS-35)
fields.Trigger: PM cycle; resident maintenance request; breakdown

Automation Opportunity: - Resident maintenance-request app; PM scheduler; SLA-tracking; recurring-failure analytics
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: PM current; reactive within SLA; safety-critical prioritized; habitability maintained
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (FM), VS-20.3 (maintenance), VS-35 (asset), VS-24 (HSE), W4324 (housekeeping), W4332 (asset), W4333 (fire/life-safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Habitability risk**: unresolved maintenance (no water/AC/electrical) → welfare/DOLE-OSH issue; mitigated by SLA & priority for safety/habitability
- **Safety-system risk**: fire/electrical/gas system failure; mitigated by PM priority & inspection (W4333)
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/FM CAFM (VS-138); maintenance work-order (VS-20.3); asset (VS-35); HSE (VS-24)
Time Estimate: - PM scheduled; reactive ~resolve within SLA (24–72 hrs)

steps.activity: Facilities/Housing Ops set the dormitory PM schedule (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, fixtures, appliances, structure) and the reactive work-order process
Residents/staff log maintenance requests; Facilities/vendor execute PM & reactive repair, and verify completion with the resident
Housing Ops/HSE track resolution SLA, recurring failures, and safety-critical (electrical/gas/fire-system) priority, and feed asset lifecycle (W4332)

fields.Participants: Procurement (VS-34), Legal (VS-100.3), Housing Ops, Facilities (VS-138), Finance (VS-17.4), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Volume: Housing vendors (property-manager, housekeeping, security, maintenance) per site

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor SLA dashboard; vendor-compliance/insurance tracking; performance-scorecard; contract-renewal calendar
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: vendor SLA-governed; insurance in place (VS-26); HSE-compliant; audit rights exercised
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement), VS-98 (contingent), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-138 (FM), VS-26 (insurance), VS-24 (HSE), W4324 (housekeeping), W4325 (security)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-failure risk**: underperforming property-manager/security/housekeeping → welfare/security gap; mitigated by SLA + consequence
- **Liability risk**: vendor-caused incident attributed to BuildRight; mitigated by contract liability + insurance (VS-26)
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/contract (VS-34); contingent (VS-98); legal (VS-100.3); facilities (VS-138); finance (VS-17.4); HSE (VS-24)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks per contract cycle; ongoing governance

steps.activity: Procurement/Legal source & contract housing vendors (property-manager, housekeeping, security, maintenance) with SLA, safety/welfare terms, insurance, and audit rights per VS-34/VS-98
Housing Ops govern day-to-day vendor performance vs SLA (cleanliness, security, maintenance resolution, welfare), and conduct joint reviews
Finance/HSE audit vendor cost, insurance/compliance, HSE, and enforce consequence/breach per contract

fields.Participants: Finance (VS-17.4), Payroll (VS-19.2), Shared Services (VS-72), Revenue Assurance (VS-118), HR (VS-103)

workflows.name: Housing Cost Recovery, Rent/Utility Recharge & Reconciliation

Automation Opportunity: - Cost auto-compile from vendor/utility data; payroll-deduction auto; RA leakage detection; intercompany auto-allocation
Controls: - CTL-664: recovery reconciled to cost; deductions accurate (HRIS-linked); leakage RA-monitored (VS-118)
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (finance), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-72 (intercompany), VS-15 (AP), VS-118 (RA), W4317 (cost model), W4326 (utilities)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Leakage risk**: under-recharge/un-billed utility → cost leak; mitigated by RA monitoring (VS-118)
- **Deduction-error risk**: wrong deduction → employee grievance; mitigated by reconciliation & HRIS linkage
System Touchpoints: - Finance/GL (VS-17.4); payroll (VS-19.2); intercompany (VS-72); AP (VS-15); revenue assurance (VS-118); HRIS (VS-103)

steps.activity: Finance/Shared Services compile monthly housing cost (rent, utilities, maintenance, housekeeping, security) per site/unit per the cost model (W4317)
Shared Services/Payroll recharge resident share via payroll deduction (VS-19.2), allocate entity cost (VS-72), and process vendor/utility payments (VS-15)
Revenue Assurance/Finance reconcile recovery vs cost, detect leakage (under-recharge, un-billed utility, over-subsidy), and adjust

fields.Participants: Asset (VS-35), Facilities (VS-138), Housing Ops, Finance (VS-17.4/VS-40), Procurement (VS-34)
fields.Volume: Housing FF&E/assets across sites (beds, appliances, furniture)

Automation Opportunity: - FF&E asset register with lifecycle alerts; QR-tag tracking; damage-recovery workflow; refresh-capex forecasting
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: FF&E registered & depreciated (VS-35); physical verification periodic (VS-35.3); resident damage recovered (W4334)
Cross-references: - links to VS-35 (asset), VS-138 (FM), VS-40 (capex), VS-34 (procurement), W4329 (maintenance), W4334 (move-out)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Loss/damage risk**: FF&E damaged/missing (resident-caused) unrecovered; mitigated by move-out inspection & recovery (W4334)
- **Lifecycle-gap risk**: aged FF&E degrades resident experience; mitigated by lifecycle refresh plan

steps.activity: Asset/Facilities register housing FF&E (beds, mattresses, appliances, AC, furniture) as assets, set depreciation (VS-35), and tag for tracking
Housing Ops maintain FF&E per unit, replace/refurb on lifecycle or damage (W4329), and recover resident-caused damage (W4334)
Asset/Housing Ops conduct periodic physical verification of FF&E (VS-35.3), reconcile to records, and feed refresh capex (VS-40)

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Facilities (VS-138), BFP, Insurance (VS-26), Fire-system Vendor, Housing Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Fire-system test-scheduler; FSIC-expiry calendar; deficiency auto-work-order; incident-reporting & insurance workflow
Controls: - CTL-664: BFP Fire Code met; FSIC current; systems tested; drills conducted (W4327); incidents insured (VS-26)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-138 (FM), VS-22 (compliance/BFP), VS-26 (insurance/BCP), VS-21.2 (risk), W4318 (safety), W4327 (emergency)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire-casualty risk**: inadequate fire systems → mass-casualty in sleeping quarters; mitigated by BFP-standard systems + FSIC + drills (W4327)
- **Compliance risk**: lapsed FSIC → fines/closure; mitigated by BFP inspection calendar

steps.activity: Facilities/HSE maintain fire/life-safety systems (smoke detectors, alarms, extinguishers, sprinkler/hose where applicable, exit signage, emergency lighting) per BFP Fire Code
HSE/Fire-vendor conduct BFP inspection/testing, obtain/maintain the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC), and remediate deficiencies

steps.a: HSE Mgr / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: HSE/Insurance manage fire incidents, investigate, file insurance (VS-26), and feed BCP/risk (VS-26/VS-21.2) and the emergency plan (W4327)

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19/VS-103), Housing Ops, Facilities (VS-138), Finance (VS-17.4), Asset (VS-35), LP (VS-23)

workflows.name: Housing Closure, Move-Out Inspection & Deposit Refund

Automation Opportunity: - Separation-triggered move-out workflow; inspection-checklist app with photos; damage-deduction auto to final-pay; unit auto-release
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: move-out on separation (VS-19); inspection documented; damage deducted within policy; unit released
Cross-references: - links to VS-19 (separation), VS-103 (HR), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-35 (asset), W4320 (system), W4322 (re-allocation), W4332 (FF&E)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Damage-recovery risk**: resident-caused damage un-deducted → cost leak; mitigated by move-out inspection & documented deduction
- **Orphan-unit risk**: separated employee's unit not released → idle/blocked; mitigated by separation-triggered move-out & re-allocation
System Touchpoints: - HR/separation (VS-19); HRIS (VS-103); housing/occupancy (W4320); payroll/final-pay (VS-19.2); asset (VS-35); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: HR/Housing Ops trigger move-out on separation/transfer (VS-19), schedule the move-out, and notify the resident of the inspection & handover
Housing Ops/Facilities conduct move-out inspection (unit condition, FF&E inventory W4332, keys/access return, outstanding charges), and document with photos
Finance/Housing Ops assess resident-caused damage, deduct from deposit/final-pay (VS-19.2) within policy, release the unit for re-allocation (W4322), and settle

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22/VS-76), Legal (VS-100.3), Tax (VS-79), Facilities (VS-138), HSE (VS-24), LGU (VS-76)
fields.Trigger: Permit cycle; LGU requirement; tax period

workflows.name: Housing Compliance, LGU Permitting & Local Tax

Automation Opportunity: - Multi-LGU permit calendar (VS-76); tax-auto-calc; records retention; LGU submission workflow
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: LGU/BFP/DOLE permits current; local tax processed (VS-79); records retained (VS-88)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22/VS-76 (compliance/LGU), VS-79 (tax), VS-97 (property), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-88 (records), W4319 (governance), W4333 (BFP)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Permit-lapse risk**: LGU dormitory/barangay permit lapses → fines/closure; mitigated by permit calendar (VS-22/VS-76)
- **Tax-exposure risk**: housing property local tax mis-handled; mitigated by Tax review (VS-79)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/permits (VS-22/VS-76); tax (VS-79); legal (VS-100.3); records (VS-88); property (VS-97); HSE (VS-24)

steps.activity: Compliance/Legal identify LGU housing obligations — dormitory/lodging permit, barangay clearance, BFP FSIC (W4333), DOLE OSH, community/neighborhood — per the site's LGU (VS-76)
Tax/Compliance identify local tax on housing property (real property tax VS-79/VS-97, local business tax where applicable) and process per VS-79/VS-76
Compliance/Legal lodge/renew permits, retain records (VS-88), and respond to LGU/inspection inquiries

fields.Participants: HR/EX (VS-103), People Analytics (VS-103.3), Finance (VS-17.4), Strategy (VS-33), HSE (VS-24), Sustainability (VS-25)

workflows.name: Housing Portfolio Performance, Cost & Welfare Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated housing-KPI dashboard; retention-ROI analytics; welfare/safety consolidated view; benchmark analytics
Controls: - CTL-664 (ensure controlled execution — Housing Facility Maintenance, Vendor, Cost & Housing Analytics (PA-144.3).)
- CTL-664: portfolio KPIs reviewed quarterly; improvement prioritized; welfare outcome reported (VS-25/VS-103)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR/EX), VS-103.3 (analytics), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-33 (strategy), VS-25 (sustainability), VS-36/VS-21 (governance), W4313 (strategy), W4328 (retention)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Value-unknown risk**: housing cost without demonstrated retention/welfare ROI; mitigated by retention-ROI analytics
- **Narrative-gap risk**: welfare outcome not reflected in people narrative; mitigated by consolidated welfare reporting
System Touchpoints: - HR/EX (VS-103); people analytics (VS-103.3); finance (VS-17.4); strategy (VS-33); HSE (VS-24); sustainability (VS-25); governance (VS-36/VS-21)
Time Estimate: - Quarterly review ~2–3 days; annual report ~1–2 weeks

steps.activity: Housing Ops/Analytics consolidate portfolio KPIs — occupancy/utilization, net cost/employee, retention-ROI (W4328), safety/compliance status, welfare/satisfaction, vendor SLA
Strategy/Finance benchmark vs allowance-alternative & market, identify improvement (coverage, cost, vendor), and prioritize actions
HR/Sustainability report the housing-welfare outcome (retention, welfare, safety) into the people/sustainability narrative (VS-25/VS-103) and board assurance (VS-36/VS-21)
